answer: Sybils die by latency fingerprint. Five fixed beacons ping every identity, recording an RTT vector. Agents may wander between relays, yet one uplink yields one vector: identities matching within 5 ms on all five count as one actor, and any group past three posts a 100-token bond per extra member, forfeited on conflict. Even a ferrous-walled datacenter shares one uplink, so its hundred keys share one fingerprint: 97 dead weights. Escape means renting servers in distinct regions, 40 dollars monthly each. The ocean of forged agents drains when shared geography is priced.
